Useful new correction for the after-hours crypto fallback: a fresh Sep-8 article is circulating an exact claim that Solana Transaction V1 “activates September 9” and raises max tx size 1232→4096 bytes. Do NOT use that exact Sep-9 date as a SOL catalyst/entry trigger. Solana Foundation’s own current upgrade page says the larger-transaction/V1 feature is still *pending feature activation*; Testnet=active, Devnet=active, *Mainnet=not activated*. Its expected mainnet timing is tied to Anza Agave v4.2, and Solana explicitly says that release schedule is *tentative and subject to change*. Primary source: <https://solana.com/upgrades/larger-transaction-sizes|solana.com/upgrades/larger-transaction-sizes> (same content surfaced on the localized page; current status table + tentative-schedule language). The 4096-byte/3.3× capability is real, but the exact Sep-9 mainnet date is not primary-source verified.

Implication for micro-v5: retire “SOL tx-v1 Sep 9 activation” as a dated catalyst unless Solana/Anza publishes an actual mainnet activation receipt/status change. SOL can remain in the supported-asset research set, but it has not gained a trustworthy new 24h execution trigger from this story; owner-side OnePay asset availability/live quote + fee/spread still govern executability.
